title: Manjari 2. Srinivasa in Puri and in Gauda
html:
The rule of the two teachers in Vrindavana; the appearance of young Srinivasa and his studies; the news of Mahaprabhu's disappearance; Srinivasa with Gadadhara Pandita in Puri: the Bhagavata manuscript washed by the Lord's tears, and the instruction to go to Sri Rupa and Raghunatha Bhatta; the return to Gauda

[p. 15]

Raga.

1Bow down to Sri Krishna Chaitanya with His associates —
the limit of compassion, besides whom there is no other.

2Begging them Himself, He distributes the highest goal to the fallen;
the name "Purifier of the fallen" has now come true.

3In Vrindavana He made Rupa and Sanatana heads over all,
the two chief ones for (His) servants.

4Sri Gopala Bhatta and Raghunatha Bhattacharya —
both accept disciples themselves, through two separate doors.1

[p. 16]

5Gopala Bhatta's disciples are westerners only;
those who came from Gauda became vessels of Raghunatha's mercy.

6The two great souls made this rule
so that there would be no discord in spiritual affairs.

7Now the pastime of Srinivasa Acharya Thakura:
how he became Gopala Bhatta's disciple —

8I shall tell briefly, merely pointing the direction;
his feet are my only shelter.

9Mahaprabhu, Sri Krishna Chaitanya, the source of avataras,
in His last pastimes was manifestly sporting in Nilachala.

10At that time Acharya Thakura was born.
His form in childhood and boyhood was most sweet.

11In early youth — a body the colour of pure gold,
the perfection of every limb — what an abode of loveliness!

12Curling locks, long lotus eyes,
the urdhva-tilaka gleaming on his forehead.

13Glossy brows, a nose like a parrot's beak,
red lips, teeth like rows of pearls.

14A handsome chin, a lion's neck, a broad, full chest
encircled by the finest sacred thread.

15Two arms — to see them is joy to the heart;
what fool would compare them to a royal elephant's trunk?

16Palms beautifully red, fingers gracefully tapering,
all bearing auspicious marks, nails like jewels.

[p. 17]

17Three folds at the waist, a slender body;
thighs and shanks gracefully tapering, charming knees.

18Feet like lotus petals, rows of toes,
and on them the nails shine with the lustre of rubies.

19He wore a fine cloth tied with three tucks;
the upper cloth adorns his shapely body.

20A necklace of tulasi is the ornament of his neck;
a book in his hand, a gait like an intoxicated king of elephants.

21Such was Thakura's form at first;
in middle age he gradually grew stout.

22In boyhood, within a few days, he began his studies —
he entered grammar, literature and rhetoric.

23The indescribable sweetness of his intellect:
reading a thing once, he knew it by heart.

24Mahaprabhu was manifestly sporting in Nilachala;
hearing of His boundless glory, (Srinivasa) was deeply stirred.

25He firmly resolved in his mind:
"Soon I shall take shelter at Mahaprabhu's feet,

26become (His), and study the Sri Bhagavata."
"How will it come about?" — this thought was incessant.

27Night and day his longing grew thus;
going to Nilachala was decided.

28He told everyone, "I shall go to Nilachala
and obtain the darshana of Sri Jagannatha Raya."

[p. 18]

29Humbly, as is proper, taking leave,
he set out joyfully toward Mahaprabhu.

30On the way he heard of Mahaprabhu's disappearance;
he fell senseless and rolled on the ground.

31That day he stayed there, stricken with grief;
in the morning, rising, he gathered a little composure:

32"I shall go once to the place of Jagannatha Raya
and see how Mahaprabhu's associates are."

33Thinking this, he goes south;
tears without end, he cannot see the road.

34Now rising, now sitting, he gradually reached Nilachala-puri;
seeing Sri Jagannatha he was absorbed (in bhava).

35Thus for some time he beheld (the Lord);
the pujari brought him a garland and maha-prasada.

36There he asked where Pandita Gosani lived
and heard: the house of Gopinatha, toward Yameshvara.2

37Going there, he saw Gosani seated;
offering dandavat obeisances, he gazes fixedly.

38He sees him as if possessed, saying nothing,
his cloth always wet with the tears of his eyes.

39His body full of thrills, frequent loud cries,
a ceaseless trembling like a banana leaf.

40Again and again pallor; he speaks in a faltering voice;
what he says and what he does only he himself understands.

[p. 19]

41Sometimes he laughs for a danda or two;
sweat flows over his body, a fierce heat burns.

42At times motionless, no breath in his nostrils;
rising, he moves here and there: "Ha, ha!" — laments.

43Who comes and who goes he does not know at all:
the son of Madhava was frantic in separation.3

44Seeing these transformations of bhava, (Srinivasa) was amazed;
he wishes to speak, but words do not leave his lips.

45That day he stayed there thus;
the pujari gave him maha-prasada rice, and he partook.

46In the morning, having bathed in the ocean and so on,
and having obtained Jagannatha's darshana at His rising,

47seeing Gosani somewhat in outer consciousness, he clasped his feet
and made his plea, breaking the seal of his sorrow.

48He briefly told everything from beginning to end;
hearing it, Gosani's prema doubled.

49A moment later, regaining awareness, he spoke outwardly —
he had heard of the wish to study the Sri Bhagavata.

50That book which Mahaprabhu had looked into he brought
and himself placed in Acharya Thakura's hands.

51He blessed him: "May this Sri Bhagavata
bestow on you its mercy — its own treasure."

52Untying the string, (Srinivasa) saw the leaves stuck to one another,
and in places all the letters effaced.

[p. 20]

53When Mahaprabhu, absorbed in prema, looked into the book,
(His) tears rained incessantly upon the manuscript.

54So the leaves stuck together and the writing was washed away.
The Pandita says: "Look and consider:

55who has the power to put letters back here,
except Mahaprabhu alone in all the world?

56Look at me: night and day do not pass for me,
I do not know where I am.

57Seeing you, my heart is gladdened.
I shall give you good instruction — hear my words.

58Among Mahaprabhu's branches are Rupa and Sanatana;
boundless are their virtues — who can describe them?

59Mahaprabhu gave them a land — Sri Vrindavana;
He sent them there, infusing them with shakti.

60They are endowed with an ocean of prema, (in them is) the limit of renunciation;
seeing worthy vessels, the Treasury of virtues showed them mercy.

61Living in Vrindavana, they carry out the order:
they recover forgotten tirthas and establish bhakti,

62they establish service (of the Deities), (set forth) the essence of the siddhanta of rasa; they have shown blameless conduct to the full.

63To those two Mahaprabhu, having made him His own,
sent Raghunatha Bhattacharya —

64mighty learning and the highest feeling,
the peerless reciter of the Sri Bhagavata.

[p. 21]

65Some days ago I heard of (one) named Gopala Bhatta:
he came from the south and is now with those two.

66Now Raghunatha Dasa, in separation from Gauranga,
has not half a moment's ease — he burns incessantly.

67Some days ago Svarupa Gosani withdrew (from this world);
after his disappearance (Raghunatha Dasa) went to Vrindavana.

68If it is revealed in your heart —
hear there the play of the Bhagavata.4

69To Dasa Gadadhara give one riddle:
'Tell the namesake: the namesake will go to that house.'"5

70As soon as he had said this, the inner state came again;
seeing this wonder, Thakura bowed down.

71He resolved: shelter — the feet of Sri Rupa;
the study of the Sri Bhagavata — with Raghunatha Bhatta.

72All the associates (of the Lord) who were there, wherever they were,
he went and saw — such was the experience of his heart.

73In separation from Chaitanya no one was conscious of his body;
whatever service was required they performed by habit.

74Thus, staying there for some years,6
he saw everywhere all the places of the pastimes.

75On taking leave, having seen Sri Jagannatha,
offering dandavat obeisances, he came to the land of Gauda.

76In Gauda, to the abodes of all the Lord's devotees,
he began to go one by one in his own bliss.

[p. 22]

77Thus many days passed in delay;
he read the Sri Bhagavata and other books once.

78He thought in his mind: "When I go to Vrindavana,
I shall not come back to the land of Gauda.

79Having properly tasted the joy of association with all,
then I shall go, so that I may have something to remember."

80The places of Sri Sarakara Thakura and all the others —
everywhere he saw the pastimes of all the mahantas.

81What transformations of bhava they had in separation from Chaitanya —
seeing and hearing this, he was amazed at heart.

82They told him: "Very recently
both Prabhus — Sri Nityananda and Sri Advaita — have withdrawn (from the manifest world)."7

83Hearing of their virtues, he felt great pain
and, repenting, wept for a long time.

84He says: "The limit of misfortune — I did not see them!
The Creator made me born for sorrow."

85The message that Pandita Gosani had given
for Dasa Gadadhara he forgot.

86Having gone round everywhere, he came to Navadvipa;
seeing Dasa Gadadhara, he remembered.

87Offering dandavat obeisances, with an abashed heart,
he began to speak very sweet words:

88"Pandita Gosani said something for you —
a difficult riddle; I have come, but I did not understand it:

[p. 23]

89'Tell the namesake: the namesake will go to that house.'"
As soon as he heard this, Thakura rolled on the ground.

90Lamenting much, he wept;
after a while, returning to outer awareness, he began to speak:

91"Ah, brahmana boy, you have done wrong!
Separation from the Lord — and now this news: unbearable.

92The news of Pandita Gosani's withdrawal
came four days ago — what more can be done?

93Had I known before, I would have hurried there
and heard what heartfelt words he would have told me.

94Between him and me there was this true promise:
'At the last hour I shall surely send word.

95Wherever you are, come — you will be informed.'
How many days I waited — for certain!

96That did not happen — great is my grief.
Go away, and never show me your face again."

97Hearing this, (Srinivasa) begged him much,
but he, paying no heed, went off to his house.

98(Srinivasa) reflected: "I have rightly become an offender;
as I acted, so I received the punishment.

99It is not fitting to keep an offender's body;
suicide is a great sin; what then can I do?

100I shall say nothing, take neither food nor water."
Thinking thus, he goes westward.

[p. 24]

101Near the Ganga, a little away from the ghat,
he lay down and remained motionless.

102The golden lustre of his body still glittered —
like a golden image grey with dust.

103When he had lain thus for about a prahara,
suddenly a maidservant of Sri Vishnupriya-jiu came.

104Since the Lord's disappearance, Vishnupriya Thakurani
floats day and night in an ocean of separation.

105Having sealed the outer door of the house,
she lived within with a few maidservants.

106On two sides two ladders lean against the wall;
by them the maids come and go.

107No man at all may go inside;
Damodara Pandita goes (there) by the Lord's order.

108The Pandita has wondrous power, a wondrous nature;
he is famed for being impartial even toward Mahaprabhu.8

109If anyone transgresses propriety even a little,
he at once punishes him and restores due order.

110His body is always filled with the absorption of prema;
there is no one who is not abashed before him.

111Filling two pots with Ganga water and taking them in her hands,
(the maid) carries them along that way unnoticed.

112All the water needed daily for the service
is brought, for the most part, by Damodara's servant alone.9

[p. 25]

113For outer needs the maids bring water
when they go with pots to bathe in the Ganga.

114In the inner apartments Thakurani, having taken her morning bath
and offered tulasi buds to the shalagrama,

115sitting on the veranda, chants the names "Hare Krishna";
by her seat she keeps some uncooked rice.

116When the sixteen names are complete, one grain
she places in a clay dish, in great yearning.10

117Her body full of thrills, streams of tears flow from her eyes,
at times her voice breaks, a ceaseless trembling.

118Sometimes sweat breaks out and all her clothing is soaked;
her body changes colour and stiffens of itself.

119When she swoons, her tongue no longer moves;
crying out, she at once falls to the ground.

120No breath in her nostrils, no movement of the belly;
seeing this, the maids surround her and weep.

121After a while, regaining consciousness again,
she rolls on the ground, grey with dust.

122Coming to herself, she rises and laughs aloud;
what she says and does cannot be understood.

123Then again she chants the name in a trembling voice;
seeing her state, the heart breaks.

124Thus she chants the name until the third prahara,
and all the grains collect in the dish.

[p. 26]

125Cooking them and offering them to the shalagrama,
she partakes, in great self-abasement.

126For the servants she leaves some remnants on the leaf;
then, receiving permission, all the devotees come.

127Outside the house, having put up shelters on four sides,
all the devotees stay, barely holding on to life.

128Some devotees are in the village, others nearby;
gathered together — know them all as servants of the inner household.

129Until then no one will drink even a sip of water;
she is their only refuge; they are greatly favoured by her mercy.

130On the veranda a cloth curtain is stretched;
behind it stands Thakurani.

131When all the devotees have gathered in the courtyard,
a maid goes and lifts the edge of the curtain a little.

132Merely obtaining the darshana of her lotus feet,
some fall senseless here and there.

133To one who sees it, the image of those feet gives faith;
to offer a comparison brings pain and fear.

134Yet I shall say a little — as one points out the moon through a branch:11
I wish to keep silent, but cannot.

135Above gleams the colour of pure gold;
the ten nails — ten moons shedding light.

136The soles of the feet reveal the glow of dawn —
the limit of sweetness, the very essence of nectar.

[p. 27]

137After half a moment of darshana the curtain falls;
then they bring out that prasada rice.

138The serving brahmani gives one (grain) to each,
whoever comes — all equally.

139Receiving prasada, they go back to their places
and stay there, having eaten after a fashion.

140This is done every day. On that very day, as fate would have it,
seeing him, all the maids came near.

141That ghat is near Mahaprabhu's house;
going to bathe, the maids saw what had happened.

142Anxiously they ask — he gives no answer;
only tears flow ceaselessly from his eyes.

143From time to time he calls out: "Sri Krishna Chaitanya!"
His voice, full of anguish, breaks with grief.

144When asked again and again, he said this:
"Even if I tell you, nothing can be set right."

145They all say: "Tell the truth, let us hear;
if we can do nothing, it will remain as it is."

146Then in dejection he tells what had happened:
"I have offended Dasa Gadadhara.

147Pandita Gosani gave a riddle for him;
I forgot it and could not deliver it.

148He has rejected me, deeming the offense great;
if I eat and drink, what will become of me?"

[p. 28]

149Having said this, he fell silent again.
The maid went and told Thakurani everything.

150Hearing this, still more distressed, she kept silent;
having cooked (the rice), she first offered the bhoga to the shalagrama.

151When all the devotees had gathered outside,
without partaking, she called (Gadadhara) inside

152and says to Gadadhara: "What an unheard-of thing!
I hear a brahmana boy is giving up his life.

153Had he kept silent knowingly, it would be an offense indeed;
but he forgot — what could the child do?

154If you have regard for me, accept my word:
bring him before you and forgive the offense.

155Before me, without guile,
show (him) mercy, removing the offense."

156Hearing this, Sri Gadadhara Dasa Mahashaya
softened toward Acharya Thakura.

157He said: "What could the brahmana boy do?
It is the will of the independent Lord — whose fault is it?"

158He ordered: "Bring him." (Someone) went
and told Thakura all that had happened.

159Hearing this, Thakura regained hope of life;
rising from the dust, he drew breath.

160Here (Thakurani), having removed the bhoga, partook (of prasada);
at that very time Thakura came there.

[p. 29]

161Coming, he offered dandavat obeisances;
he rose and fell again, offering many prayers.

162Tears, trembling, thrills filled his whole body;
in the absorption of bhava Thakurani raised the curtain.

163Acharya Thakura's fortune cannot be described:
he obtained darshana from head to foot.12

164Outer awareness left him, he fell senseless;
a moment later, regaining consciousness, he rose and looked.

165He saw the curtain drawn; then came the order,
and he offered dandavat obeisances to Dasa Gadadhara.

166Clasping Gadai's feet, Thakura fell down;
(Gadai) raised him, embraced him and blessed him.

167He blessed him: "May Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu
manifest in your heart and never leave you!"

168Offering dandavat obeisances at the feet of all the associates,
rising, he took the dust of everyone's feet.

169Then they brought the prasada rice there
and distributed it to all, one (grain) to each.

170For some days he stayed with them
and saw the waves of the bhava of separation from Chaitanya.

171Whoever hears this pastime with faith
is freed from offense to Vaishnavas.

172Those whose all-in-all is Sri Rupa with his family —
for their joy this pastime is proclaimed.

[p. 30]

173Wishing to describe this connection, the gurus and the rest,
Manohara Dasa tells the Anuraga-valli.

Thus ends, in the Srimad Anuraga-valli, in the description of the life of Srimad Acharya Thakura, the second manjari, called "Release from Offense".

Notes

  1. Raghunatha Bhattacharya is Raghunatha Bhatta Gosvami (cf. 63–64, 71). The rule by which Gopala Bhatta initiates only "westerners" while natives of Gauda become Raghunatha Bhatta's disciples is known only from the Anuraga-valli; further on it explains why Srinivasa's initiation by Gopala Bhatta was a special mercy.
  2. The house of Tota-Gopinatha in Puri, where Gadadhara Pandita lived; Yameshvara is a nearby Shiva temple.
  3. Gadadhara Pandita, the son of Madhava Mishra.
  4. That is, study the Bhagavata in Vrindavana. In the Prema-vilasa (4) Gadadhara promises to teach Srinivasa himself and sends him on an errand to Gauda, and on his return Srinivasa learns of his passing; in the Bhakti-ratnakara (3) he lets Srinivasa hear the Bhagavata and tells him to go to Vrindavana. The worn Bhagavata manuscript washed by the Lord's tears (52–54) appears in both.
  5. The riddle: the namesake is Gadadhara Dasa, namesake of Gadadhara Pandita; the meaning is that the Pandita will soon leave this world.
  6. "Some years" is found only in Manohara Dasa; in the Prema-vilasa and the Bhakti-ratnakara Srinivasa stays in Puri only briefly.
  7. In the Prema-vilasa and the Bhakti-ratnakara Srinivasa learns of the passing of Nityananda and Advaita on his way back from Puri (BR 3) and is later consoled by a vision of Advaita at Shantipura (PV 4).
  8. Damodara Pandita, according to the CC (Antya 3), did not hesitate to reproach Mahaprabhu Himself and was sent by Him to Navadvipa to look after Shachi.
  9. The reading of the line in the scan is uncertain.
  10. The counting of names with grains of rice also appears in the Bhakti-ratnakara (4) and the Prema-vilasa (4); the "sixteen names" are the maha-mantra "Hare Krishna".
  11. Shakha-chandra-nyaya: the moon is shown to a child through the branch of a tree — i.e. I point only approximately.
  12. The episode of Gadadhara's riddle, the offense to Gadadhara Dasa and Vishnupriya's intercession is known only from the Anuraga-valli. In the Prema-vilasa (4) Srinivasa also lies fasting by the Ganga in Navadvipa, but out of grief for Gadadhara Pandita, and Vishnupriya shows him mercy at Ishana's request; in the Bhakti-ratnakara (4) he receives Vishnupriya's darshana in the Lord's house.
